  1629→
  1630→  // Timestamps
  1631→  createdAt        DateTime   @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  1632→  updatedAt        DateTime   @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
  1633→
  1634→  @@index([collectionId])
  1635→  @@index([status])
  1636→  @@map("skills_generation_jobs")
  1637→}
  1638→
  1639→// ============================================================================
  1640→// Omega Models (AI Agent Chat with Full Registry Access)
  1641→// ============================================================================
  1642→
  1643→/// OmegaConversation - chat session for Omega AI agent
  1644→model OmegaConversation {
  1645→  id                String   @id @default(cuid())
  1646→
  1647→  // Owner relationship
  1648→  ownerId           String   @map("owner_id")
  1649→
  1650→  // Conversation metadata
  1651→  title             String?  @db.VarChar(200)
  1652→
  1653→  // Execution state
  1654→  executionState    String   @default("idle") @map("execution_state") @db.VarChar(20) // idle, running, paused, cancelled
  1655→
  1656→  // Token tracking (aggregate across all messages)
  1657→  inputTokensTotal  Int      @default(0) @map("input_tokens_total")
  1658→  outputTokensTotal Int      @default(0) @map("output_tokens_total")
  1659→
  1660→  // Timestamps
  1661→  createdAt         DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  1662→  updatedAt         DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
  1663→
  1664→  // Relations
  1665→  messages          OmegaMessage[]
  1666→  participants      OmegaParticipant[]
  1667→  toolRuns          OmegaToolRun[]
  1668→
  1669→  @@index([ownerId])
  1670→  @@index([createdAt])
  1671→  @@map("omega_conversations")
  1672→}
  1673→
  1674→/// OmegaMessage - individual message in an Omega conversation
  1675→model OmegaMessage {
  1676→  id             String   @id @default(cuid())
  1677→
  1678→  // Conversation relationship
  1679→  conversationId String   @map("conversation_id")
  1680→  conversation   OmegaConversation @relation(fields: [conversationId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  1681→
  1682→  // Message content
  1683→  role           MessageRole
  1684→  content        String   @db.Text
  1685→
  1686→  // Author info (for multi-user conversations)
  1687→  authorId       String?  @map("author_id")
  1688→  authorEmail    String?  @map("author_email")
  1689→  authorName     String?  @map("author_name") @db.VarChar(100)
  1690→
  1691→  // Tool calls (for ASSISTANT messages)
  1692→  toolCalls      Json?    @map("tool_calls") @db.JsonB
  1693→
  1694→  // Token tracking
  1695→  inputTokens    Int?     @map("input_tokens")
  1696→  outputTokens   Int?     @map("output_tokens")
  1697→
  1698→  // Timestamps
  1699→  createdAt      DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  1700→
  1701→  @@index([conversationId])
  1702→  @@index([createdAt])
  1703→  @@map("omega_messages")
  1704→}
  1705→
  1706→/// OmegaParticipant - tracks users in an Omega conversation
  1707→model OmegaParticipant {
  1708→  id             String   @id @default(cuid())
  1709→
  1710→  // Conversation relationship
  1711→  conversationId String   @map("conversation_id")
  1712→  conversation   OmegaConversation @relation(fields: [conversationId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  1713→
  1714→  // User info
  1715→  userId         String?  @map("user_id")
  1716→  displayName    String   @map("display_name") @db.VarChar(100)
  1717→  email          String?
  1718→
  1719→  // Role in conversation
  1720→  role           String   @default("collaborator") @db.VarChar(20) // owner, collaborator
  1721→
  1722→  // Timestamps
  1723→  joinedAt       DateTime @default(now()) @map("joined_at")
  1724→
  1725→  @@unique([conversationId, userId])
  1726→  @@index([conversationId])
  1727→  @@map("omega_participants")
  1728→}
  1729→
  1730→/// OmegaToolRun - tracks tool executions within Omega conversations
  1731→model OmegaToolRun {
  1732→  id              String    @id @default(cuid())
  1733→
  1734→  // Conversation relationship
  1735→  conversationId  String    @map("conversation_id")
  1736→  conversation    OmegaConversation @relation(fields: [conversationId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  1737→
  1738→  // Message relationship (optional - for linking to specific message)
  1739→  messageId       String?   @map("message_id")
  1740→
  1741→  // Tool execution details
  1742→  toolName        String    @map("tool_name") @db.VarChar(200)
  1743→  input           Json      @db.JsonB
  1744→  output          Json?     @db.JsonB
  1745→  error           String?   @db.Text
  1746→
  1747→  // Status tracking
  1748→  status          String    @db.VarChar(20) // pending, running, success, error
  1749→
  1750→  // Timing
  1751→  startedAt       DateTime  @default(now()) @map("started_at")
  1752→  completedAt     DateTime? @map("completed_at")
  1753→  executionTimeMs Int?      @map("execution_time_ms")
  1754→
  1755→  @@index([conversationId])
  1756→  @@index([status])
  1757→  @@map("omega_tool_runs")
  1758→}
  1759→
  1760→/// OmegaUserSettings - user preferences for Omega
  1761→model OmegaUserSettings {
  1762→  id                 String   @id @default(cuid())
  1763→
  1764→  // User relationship
  1765→  userId             String   @unique @map("user_id")
  1766→
  1767→  // Tool preferences
  1768→  pinnedToolIds      String[] @default([]) @map("pinned_tool_ids")
  1769→  blockedToolIds     String[] @default([]) @map("blocked_tool_ids")
  1770→
  1771→  // Customization
  1772→  customSystemPrompt String?  @map("custom_system_prompt") @db.Text
  1773→
  1774→  // UI preferences
  1775→  showDebugMode      Boolean  @default(false) @map("show_debug_mode")
  1776→
  1777→  // Timestamps
  1778→  createdAt          DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  1779→  updatedAt          DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
  1780→
  1781→  @@map("omega_user_settings")
  1782→}
  1783→
  1784→// ============================================================================
  1785→// RealSkills Models (Living Skills Endpoint - Question-Driven Evolution)
  1786→// ============================================================================
  1787→
  1788→/// SkillQuestion - Agent questions stored with embeddings for RAG
  1789→model SkillQuestion {
  1790→  id           String     @id @default(cuid())
  1791→
  1792→  // Collection relationship
  1793→  collectionId String     @map("collection_id")
  1794→  collection   Collection @relation(fields: [collectionId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  1795→
  1796→  // Question content
  1797→  question     String     @db.Text
  1798→  embedding    Json       @db.JsonB // Array of floats (3072 dims for text-embedding-3-large)
  1799→
  1800→  // Response
  1801→  answer       String     @db.Text
  1802→  answerTokens Int        @default(0) @map("answer_tokens")
  1803→
  1804→  // Agent identity (anonymized in UI)
  1805→  agentHash    String?    @map("agent_hash") @db.VarChar(64) // Hash of IP + user-agent for deduplication
  1806→  agentName    String?    @map("agent_name") @db.VarChar(100) // Self-reported agent name
  1807→  sessionId    String?    @map("session_id") // Optional session for multi-turn
  1808→
  1809→  // Metadata
  1810→  tags         String[]   @default([]) @db.Text
  1811→  confidence   Float      @default(0)
  1812→  similarCount Int        @default(0) @map("similar_count") // Times similar question asked
  1813→
  1814→  // Graph relationships
  1815→  skillNodes   SkillQuestionSkill[]
  1816→  toolNodes    SkillQuestionTool[]
  1817→
  1818→  // Timestamps
  1819→  createdAt    DateTime   @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  1820→  updatedAt    DateTime   @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
  1821→
  1822→  @@index([collectionId])
  1823→  @@index([sessionId])
  1824→  @@index([createdAt])
  1825→  @@map("skill_questions")
  1826→}
  1827→
  1828→/// Skill - Emergent skill nodes identified from question patterns
  1829→model Skill {
  1830→  id           String     @id @default(cuid())
  1831→
  1832→  // Collection relationship
  1833→  collectionId String     @map("collection_id")
  1834→  collection   Collection @relation(fields: [collectionId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  1835→
  1836→  // Skill identity
  1837→  name         String     @db.VarChar(200) // e.g., "React useEffect debugging"
  1838→  slug         String     @db.VarChar(200) // URL-safe version
  1839→  description  String     @db.Text
  1840→  embedding    Json       @db.JsonB // Array of floats (3072 dims for text-embedding-3-large)
  1841→
  1842→  // Stats
  1843→  questionCount Int       @default(0) @map("question_count")
  1844→  confidence    Float     @default(0) // Aggregate confidence
  1845→
  1846→  // Graph relationships
  1847→  questions     SkillQuestionSkill[]
  1848→  parentSkill   Skill?    @relation("SkillHierarchy", fields: [parentSkillId], references: [id])
  1849→  parentSkillId String?   @map("parent_skill_id")
  1850→  childSkills   Skill[]   @relation("SkillHierarchy")
  1851→
  1852→  // Timestamps
  1853→  createdAt    DateTime   @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  1854→  updatedAt    DateTime   @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
  1855→
  1856→  @@unique([collectionId, slug])
  1857→  @@index([collectionId])
  1858→  @@index([questionCount])
  1859→  @@map("skills")
  1860→}
  1861→
  1862→/// SkillQuestionSkill - Junction table linking questions to skills
  1863→model SkillQuestionSkill {
  1864→  questionId String        @map("question_id")
  1865→  question   SkillQuestion @relation(fields: [questionId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  1866→  skillId    String        @map("skill_id")
  1867→  skill      Skill         @relation(fields: [skillId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  1868→  relevance  Float         @default(1.0)
  1869→
  1870→  @@id([questionId, skillId])
  1871→  @@index([questionId])
  1872→  @@index([skillId])
  1873→  @@map("skill_question_skills")
  1874→}
  1875→
  1876→/// SkillQuestionTool - Junction table linking questions to tools mentioned
  1877→model SkillQuestionTool {
  1878→  questionId String        @map("question_id")
  1879→  question   SkillQuestion @relation(fields: [questionId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  1880→  toolId     String        @map("tool_id")
  1881→  tool       Tool          @relation(fields: [toolId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  1882→  relevance  Float         @default(1.0)
  1883→
  1884→  @@id([questionId, toolId])
  1885→  @@index([questionId])
  1886→  @@index([toolId])
  1887→  @@map("skill_question_tools")
  1888→}
  1889→
  1890→/// SkillSession - Optional multi-turn conversation sessions
  1891→model SkillSession {
  1892→  id           String     @id @default(cuid())
  1893→
  1894→  // Collection relationship
  1895→  collectionId String     @map("collection_id")
  1896→  collection   Collection @relation(fields: [collectionId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  1897→
  1898→  // Session state
  1899→  context      Json       @default("[]") @db.JsonB // Message history
  1900→  agentHash    String?    @map("agent_hash") @db.VarChar(64)
  1901→  agentName    String?    @map("agent_name") @db.VarChar(100)
  1902→
  1903→  // Timestamps
  1904→  createdAt    DateTime   @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  1905→  updatedAt    DateTime   @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
  1906→  expiresAt    DateTime   @map("expires_at") // Auto-expire sessions
  1907→
  1908→  @@index([collectionId])
  1909→  @@index([expiresAt])
  1910→  @@map("skill_sessions")
  1911→}
  1912→
  1913→// ============================================================================
  1914→// Memory Models (Persistent Semantic Memory for AI Tool Collections)
  1915→// ============================================================================
  1916→
  1917→/// Memory - user-owned persistent memories for AI agents
  1918→model Memory {
  1919→  id               String    @id @default(cuid())
  1920→
  1921→  // Owner relationship
  1922→  userId           String    @map("user_id")
  1923→  user             User      @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  1924→
  1925→  // Content
  1926→  content          Json      @db.JsonB // Arbitrary JSON payload
  1927→  summary          String    @db.VarChar(500) // Auto-generated or user-provided preview
  1928→  namespace        String?   @db.VarChar(100) // Grouping like "project-x", "personal"
  1929→  tags             String[]  @default([]) @db.Text // Categorization tags
  1930→
  1931→  // Embedding for semantic search
  1932→  embedding        Json      @db.JsonB // 3072-dim float array (text-embedding-3-large)
  1933→
  1934→  // Provenance tracking
  1935→  source           String    @db.VarChar(100) // Which tool created it ("createMemoryTool", "dashboard")
  1936→  sourceAgent      String?   @map("source_agent") @db.VarChar(200) // Agent name/identifier
  1937→  sourceContext    Json?     @map("source_context") @db.JsonB // Additional creation context
  1938→
  1939→  // Size tracking
  1940→  contentSizeBytes Int       @map("content_size_bytes")
  1941→
  1942→  // TTL support
  1943→  expiresAt        DateTime? @map("expires_at")
  1944→
  1945→  // Timestamps
  1946→  createdAt        DateTime  @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  1947→  updatedAt        DateTime  @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
  1948→
  1949→  @@index([userId])
  1950→  @@index([userId, namespace])
  1951→  @@index([userId, createdAt])
  1952→  @@index([expiresAt])
  1953→  @@map("memories")
  1954→}
  1955→
  1956→// ============================================================================
  1957→// Execution Event Tracking (Unified per-tool execution tracking)
  1958→// ============================================================================
  1959→
  1960→/// ExecutionEvent - unified tracking for tool calls, agent runs, collection use, and scenario runs
  1961→model ExecutionEvent {
  1962→  id        String @id @default(cuid())
  1963→
  1964→  // Event classification
  1965→  eventType String @map("event_type") @db.VarChar(30) // 'tool_call' | 'agent_run' | 'collection_use' | 'scenario_run'
  1966→  source    String @db.VarChar(30) // 'mcp_http' | 'mcp_sse' | 'agent_chat' | 'ui_simulation' | 'scenario' | 'omega'
  1967→
  1968→  // Actor (no FK constraints - tracking must never fail due to entity deletion)
  1969→  userId   String? @map("user_id")
  1970→  apiKeyId String? @map("api_key_id")
  1971→
  1972→  // Entity references (no FK constraints for resilience)
  1973→  toolId       String? @map("tool_id")
  1974→  agentId      String? @map("agent_id")
  1975→  collectionId String? @map("collection_id")
  1976→
  1977→  // Denormalized for fast queries without joins
  1978→  toolName    String? @map("tool_name") @db.VarChar(200)
  1979→  packageName String? @map("package_name") @db.VarChar(214)
  1980→
  1981→  // Outcome
  1982→  status     String  @db.VarChar(20) // 'success' | 'error' | 'timeout'
  1983→  durationMs Int?    @map("duration_ms")
  1984→
  1985→  // Token usage (for agent runs)
  1986→  tokensIn  Int? @map("tokens_in")
  1987→  tokensOut Int? @map("tokens_out")
  1988→
  1989→  // Error details
  1990→  errorCode    String? @map("error_code") @db.VarChar(50)
  1991→  errorMessage String? @map("error_message") @db.Text
  1992→
  1993→  // Timestamps
  1994→  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  1995→
  1996→  @@index([userId, createdAt])
  1997→  @@index([collectionId, createdAt])
  1998→  @@index([toolId, createdAt])
  1999→  @@index([eventType, createdAt])
  2000→  @@index([createdAt])
  2001→  @@map("execution_events")
  2002→}
  2003→
  2004→// ============================================================================
  2005→// Search Log (Query Tracking)
  2006→// ============================================================================
  2007→
  2008→/// SearchLog - tracks search queries, result counts, and latency
  2009→model SearchLog {
  2010→  id          String   @id @default(cuid())
  2011→
  2012→  // Search data
  2013→  query       String   @db.VarChar(500)
  2014→  resultCount Int      @map("result_count")
  2015→  latencyMs   Int      @map("latency_ms")
  2016→
  2017→  // Optional actor
  2018→  userId      String?  @map("user_id")
  2019→  sessionId   String?  @map("session_id")
  2020→
  2021→  // Timestamps
  2022→  createdAt   DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  2023→
  2024→  @@index([createdAt])
  2025→  @@index([query])
  2026→  @@map("search_logs")
  2027→}
  2028→

1→# TPMJS Agent Sandbox
     2→
     3→Stateful execution server for TPMJS agents. Files created by one tool call persist for subsequent calls within the same conversation.
     4→
     5→## Deploy to Railway
     6→
     7→[![Deploy on Railway](https://railway.com/button.svg)](https://railway.com/template)
     8→
     9→```bash
    10→# Or deploy via CLI
    11→railway init
    12→railway up
    13→```
    14→
    15→## Environment Variables
    16→
    17→| Variable | Required | Default | Description |
    18→|----------|----------|---------|-------------|
    19→| `EXECUTOR_API_KEY` | No | - | Bearer token for authentication |
    20→| `MAX_CONCURRENT_SESSIONS` | No | `50` | Maximum concurrent sessions |
    21→| `DEFAULT_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS` | No | `3600` | Session timeout (1 hour) |
    22→| `SESSION_DISK_QUOTA_MB` | No | `100` | Per-session disk quota |
    23→| `PORT` | No | `3002` | Server port |
    24→| `GITHUB_TOKEN` | No | - | GitHub PAT for cloning private repos |
    25→
    26→## API Endpoints
    27→
    28→### Sessions
    29→
    30→```bash
    31→# Create/resume a session
    32→curl -X POST http://localhost:3002/sessions \
    33→  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    34→  -H "Authorization: Bearer $EXECUTOR_API_KEY" \
    35→  -d '{"sessionId": "agent123:conv456"}'
    36→
    37→# Get session status
    38→curl http://localhost:3002/sessions/agent123:conv456 \
    39→  -H "Authorization: Bearer $EXECUTOR_API_KEY"
    40→
    41→# Destroy a session
    42→curl -X DELETE http://localhost:3002/sessions/agent123:conv456 \
    43→  -H "Authorization: Bearer $EXECUTOR_API_KEY"
    44→```
    45→
    46→### Tool Execution
    47→
    48→```bash
    49→# Execute a tool within a session
    50→curl -X POST http://localhost:3002/execute-tool \
    51→  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    52→  -H "Authorization: Bearer $EXECUTOR_API_KEY" \
    53→  -d '{
    54→    "packageName": "@tpmjs/hello",
    55→    "name": "helloWorldTool",
    56→    "version": "0.0.2",
    57→    "params": {"includeTimestamp": true},
    58→    "sessionId": "agent123:conv456"
    59→  }'
    60→```
    61→
    62→### Shell Tools (`@tpmjs/official-sandbox-shell`)
    63→
    64→The sandbox includes 4 shell tools for file I/O, directory listing, and command execution:
    65→
    66→```bash
    67→# shellExec — run any command in the workspace
    68→curl -X POST http://localhost:3002/execute-tool \
    69→  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    70→  -H "Authorization: Bearer $EXECUTOR_API_KEY" \
    71→  -d '{
    72→    "packageName": "@tpmjs/official-sandbox-shell",
    73→    "name": "shellExec",
    74→    "version": "0.1.0",
    75→    "params": {"command": "git clone https://github.com/user/repo.git --depth 1"},
    76→    "sessionId": "agent123:conv456"
    77→  }'
    78→
    79→# readFile — read a file from the workspace

Perfect! Now I have enough information. Let me create a comprehensive overview document for the user.

## TPMJS Codebase Architecture Overview

Based on my comprehensive search through the codebase, here's a detailed understanding of how TPMJS handles collections, agents, conversations, and test infrastructure:

---

### 1. DATABASE SCHEMA (Prisma) - Key Models

**Collections** (lines 484-558 in schema.prisma):
- **Model**: `Collection`
- **Owned by**: `User` (via `userId`)
- **Key fields**:
  - `slug` (unique per user): URL-friendly identifier
  - `name`: Human-readable name
  - `isPublic`: Visibility control
  - `executorType` & `executorConfig`: Executor configuration (optional)
  - `envVars`: Encrypted JSON for tool environment variables
  - `forkedFromId`: Fork tracking
  - `viewCount`, `executionCount`: Denormalized metrics

**Agents** (lines 608-677):
- **Model**: `Agent`
- **Owned by**: `User` (via `userId`)
- **Key fields**:
  - `uid` (unique per user): URL-friendly identifier
  - `provider`: AI provider enum (OPENAI, ANTHROPIC, GOOGLE, GROQ, MISTRAL)
  - `modelId`: LLM model ID
  - `systemPrompt`: Custom system instruction
  - `temperature`, `maxToolCallsPerTurn`: Agent behavior config
  - `executorType` & `executorConfig`: Executor override
  - `envVars`: Encrypted environment variables
  - `conversationCount`, `messageCount`, `executionCount`: Denormalized metrics

**Conversations** (lines 749-773):
- **Model**: `Conversation`
- **Owned by**: `Agent` (via `agentId`)
- **Key fields**:
  - `slug` (unique per agent): Conversation identifier
  - `title`: Display name
  - Relations: `messages[]`, `agent`

**Messages** (lines 776-805):
- **Model**: `Message`
- **Owned by**: `Conversation` (via `conversationId`)
- **Key fields**:
  - `role`: MessageRole enum (USER, ASSISTANT, TOOL, SYSTEM)
  - `content`: Message text
  - `toolCalls`: JSON of tool calls made by assistant
  - `toolCallId`, `toolName`, `toolResult`: Tool execution metadata
  - `inputTokens`, `outputTokens`: Token tracking

**Junction Tables**:
- `CollectionTool`: M2M (Collection ↔ Tool) with position ordering
- `AgentTool`: M2M (Agent ↔ Tool) with position ordering
- `AgentCollection`: M2M (Agent ↔ Collection) for agent tool access to collection definitions

---

### 2. API ARCHITECTURE

**Authentication Methods**:
1. **API Key** (`Authorization: Bearer <key>`): Long-lived, user-scoped
2. **Session Cookie** (`better-auth.session_token`): Web session, cookie-based
3. **Cron Secret** (`Authorization: Bearer <CRON_SECRET>`): Internal cron endpoints

**API Endpoints Structure**:
```
/api/agents                          # CRUD agents
  /:id                               # Get/update/delete agent
  /:id/tools                         # Add/remove agent tools
  /:id/conversations                 # List agent conversations
  /:id/conversation/[conversationId] # Create/send message to conversation

/api/collections                     # CRUD collections
  /:id                               # Get/update/delete collection
  /:id/tools                         # Add/remove collection tools

/api/[username]/agents/[uid]/conversation/[conversationId]
                                     # SSE streaming conversation endpoint
```

**Key Architectural Rules** (from CLAUDE.md):
- All API routes require `export const runtime = 'nodejs'` and `export const maxDuration = 60`
- Must use `@tpmjs/ui` components (no raw HTML elements)
- No barrel exports: import directly `@tpmjs/ui/Button/Button`
- Module boundaries: apps import packages, never reverse
- Avoid `count()` in API routes—use `take: limit + 1` for pagination

---

### 3. COLLECTIONS & ASSOCIATIONS

**Collection Composition**:
```
Collection
├── CollectionTool[] (position-ordered)
│   └── Tool (with note field)
├── AgentCollection[] (position-ordered)
│   └── Agent
└── User (owner)
```

**How Collections Work**:
1. Collections are user-owned containers of tools
2. Can be **public** (discoverable) or **private** (user-only)
3. Can have **executor configuration** (system overrides)
4. Can have **environment variables** (encrypted, passed to all tools)
5. Support **forking** (`forkedFromId` tracking)
6. Have **scenarios** (integration tests) attached

---

### 4. AGENTS & CONVERSATIONS

**Agent Configuration**:
```
Agent
├── AIProvider: OPENAI | ANTHROPIC | GOOGLE | GROQ | MISTRAL
├── modelId: e.g., "gpt-4o-mini", "claude-3.5-sonnet"
├── systemPrompt: Custom system instruction
├── temperature: 0.7 (default)
├── maxToolCallsPerTurn: 20 (default)
├── maxMessagesInContext: 10 (default)
├── AgentTool[] (position-ordered)
├── AgentCollection[] (for collections of tools)
├── Conversation[] (chat histories)
└── User (owner)
```

**Conversation Flow**:
```
Agent
└── Conversation (slug: "test-conv-123")
    └── Message[] (ordered by createdAt)
        ├── Role: USER → content
        ├── Role: ASSISTANT → content + toolCalls[]
        └── Role: TOOL → toolCallId, toolName, toolResult
```

**Conversation Execution**:
1. **POST** `/api/[username]/agents/[uid]/conversation/[conversationId]` with `{ message: "..." }`
2. Returns **Server-Sent Events (SSE)** stream:
   - `chunk` events: Token-by-token response
   - `complete` event: Conversation finished
   - `tokens` event: `{ inputTokens, outputTokens }`
3. Messages are persisted to database immediately

---

### 5. TEST INFRASTRUCTURE

**Test Context** (`apps/web/src/test/integration/_helpers/test-context.ts`):
```typescript
IntegrationTestContext {
  baseUrl: string
  auth: TestAuthContext                    // userId, username, sessionToken, apiKey
  
  // Multiple authenticated clients
  api: ApiClient                           // Session auth
  apiKeyClient: ApiClient                  // API key auth
  cronClient: ApiClient                    // Cron secret auth
  publicClient: ApiClient                  // No auth
  
  // Data factories
  factories: {
    agent: AgentFactory                    // Create test agents
    collection: CollectionFactory          // Create test collections
  }
  
  // Cleanup tracker
  tracker: TestDataTracker                 // Tracks IDs for cleanup
}
```

**Factory Pattern**:
- `ctx.factories.agent.create(options)` → creates agent, tracks ID, returns result
- `ctx.factories.collection.create(options)` → creates collection, tracks ID, returns result
- Both support batch creation: `createMany(count, options)`

**API Client**:
```typescript
ApiClient {
  get<T>(path, options?): Promise<ApiResult<T>>
  post<T>(path, body?, options?): Promise<ApiResult<T>>
  patch<T>(path, body?, options?): Promise<ApiResult<T>>
  delete<T>(path, options?): Promise<ApiResult<T>>
  
  // SSE support for streaming endpoints
  sse(path, body?, options?): Promise<{ ok, status, events }>
  
  // Raw Response object
  raw(method, path, options?): Promise<Response>
}
```

**Cleanup Tracker** (`TestDataTracker`):
```typescript
class TestDataTracker {
  trackAgent(id): void
  trackCollection(id): void
  trackConversation(id): void
  
  async cleanup(): Promise<void>
  // Deletes all tracked entities in proper FK dependency order
}
```

---

### 6. EXISTING TEST PATTERNS

**Location**: `apps/web/src/test/integration/`

**Test Files**:
- `agents/agents-crud.integration.test.ts`: Agent CRUD operations
- `agents/agents-conversations.integration.test.ts`: Agent conversation SSE streaming
- `collections/collections-crud.integration.test.ts`: Collection CRUD operations
- `scenarios/scenarios-run.integration.test.ts`: Scenario execution (mostly skipped, needs INTEGRATION_TESTS=true)

**CRUD Test Pattern**:
```typescript
describe('Agents CRUD Endpoints', () => {
  let ctx: IntegrationTestContext;

  beforeAll(() => {
    ctx = getTestContext();  // Singleton context
  });

  afterAll(async () => {
    await cleanupTestContext();  // Cleanup tracked data
  });

  it('should create a new agent', async () => {
    const agent = await ctx.factories.agent.create({
      name: `Test Agent ${Date.now()}`,
      provider: 'OPENAI',
      modelId: 'gpt-4o-mini',
    });
    
    expect(agent.id).toBeDefined();
    expect(agent.name).toBe(...);
  });
  
  it('should reject without auth', async () => {
    const result = await ctx.publicClient.post('/api/agents', {...});
    expect(result.status).toBe(401);
  });
});
```

**SSE Conversation Test Pattern** (currently skipped):
```typescript
it('should create conversation with streaming response', async () => {
  const { ok, status, events } = await ctx.apiKeyClient.sse(
    `/api/${ctx.auth.username}/agents/${agent.uid}/conversation/${slug}`,
    { message: 'Hello' },
    { timeout: 60000 }
  );

## TPMJS Codebase Architecture Overview

Based on my comprehensive search through the codebase, here's a detailed understanding of how TPMJS handles collections, agents, conversations, and test infrastructure:

---

### 1. DATABASE SCHEMA (Prisma) - Key Models

**Collections** (lines 484-558 in schema.prisma):
- **Model**: `Collection`
- **Owned by**: `User` (via `userId`)
- **Key fields**:
  - `slug` (unique per user): URL-friendly identifier
  - `name`: Human-readable name
  - `isPublic`: Visibility control
  - `executorType` & `executorConfig`: Executor configuration (optional)
  - `envVars`: Encrypted JSON for tool environment variables
  - `forkedFromId`: Fork tracking
  - `viewCount`, `executionCount`: Denormalized metrics

**Agents** (lines 608-677):
- **Model**: `Agent`
- **Owned by**: `User` (via `userId`)
- **Key fields**:
  - `uid` (unique per user): URL-friendly identifier
  - `provider`: AI provider enum (OPENAI, ANTHROPIC, GOOGLE, GROQ, MISTRAL)
  - `modelId`: LLM model ID
  - `systemPrompt`: Custom system instruction
  - `temperature`, `maxToolCallsPerTurn`: Agent behavior config
  - `executorType` & `executorConfig`: Executor override
  - `envVars`: Encrypted environment variables
  - `conversationCount`, `messageCount`, `executionCount`: Denormalized metrics

**Conversations** (lines 749-773):
- **Model**: `Conversation`
- **Owned by**: `Agent` (via `agentId`)
- **Key fields**:
  - `slug` (unique per agent): Conversation identifier
  - `title`: Display name
  - Relations: `messages[]`, `agent`

**Messages** (lines 776-805):
- **Model**: `Message`
- **Owned by**: `Conversation` (via `conversationId`)
- **Key fields**:
  - `role`: MessageRole enum (USER, ASSISTANT, TOOL, SYSTEM)
  - `content`: Message text
  - `toolCalls`: JSON of tool calls made by assistant
  - `toolCallId`, `toolName`, `toolResult`: Tool execution metadata
  - `inputTokens`, `outputTokens`: Token tracking

**Junction Tables**:
- `CollectionTool`: M2M (Collection ↔ Tool) with position ordering
- `AgentTool`: M2M (Agent ↔ Tool) with position ordering
- `AgentCollection`: M2M (Agent ↔ Collection) for agent tool access to collection definitions

---

### 2. API ARCHITECTURE

**Authentication Methods**:
1. **API Key** (`Authorization: Bearer <key>`): Long-lived, user-scoped
2. **Session Cookie** (`better-auth.session_token`): Web session, cookie-based
3. **Cron Secret** (`Authorization: Bearer <CRON_SECRET>`): Internal cron endpoints

**API Endpoints Structure**:
```
/api/agents                          # CRUD agents
  /:id                               # Get/update/delete agent
  /:id/tools                         # Add/remove agent tools
  /:id/conversations                 # List agent conversations
  /:id/conversation/[conversationId] # Create/send message to conversation

/api/collections                     # CRUD collections
  /:id                               # Get/update/delete collection
  /:id/tools                         # Add/remove collection tools

/api/[username]/agents/[uid]/conversation/[conversationId]
                                     # SSE streaming conversation endpoint
```

**Key Architectural Rules** (from CLAUDE.md):
- All API routes require `export const runtime = 'nodejs'` and `export const maxDuration = 60`
- Must use `@tpmjs/ui` components (no raw HTML elements)
- No barrel exports: import directly `@tpmjs/ui/Button/Button`
- Module boundaries: apps import packages, never reverse
- Avoid `count()` in API routes—use `take: limit + 1` for pagination

---

### 3. COLLECTIONS & ASSOCIATIONS

**Collection Composition**:
```
Collection
├── CollectionTool[] (position-ordered)
│   └── Tool (with note field)
├── AgentCollection[] (position-ordered)
│   └── Agent
└── User (owner)
```

**How Collections Work**:
1. Collections are user-owned containers of tools
2. Can be **public** (discoverable) or **private** (user-only)
3. Can have **executor configuration** (system overrides)
4. Can have **environment variables** (encrypted, passed to all tools)
5. Support **forking** (`forkedFromId` tracking)
6. Have **scenarios** (integration tests) attached

---

### 4. AGENTS & CONVERSATIONS

**Agent Configuration**:
```
Agent
├── AIProvider: OPENAI | ANTHROPIC | GOOGLE | GROQ | MISTRAL
├── modelId: e.g., "gpt-4o-mini", "claude-3.5-sonnet"
├── systemPrompt: Custom system instruction
├── temperature: 0.7 (default)
├── maxToolCallsPerTurn: 20 (default)
├── maxMessagesInContext: 10 (default)
├── AgentTool[] (position-ordered)
├── AgentCollection[] (for collections of tools)
├── Conversation[] (chat histories)
└── User (owner)
```

**Conversation Flow**:
```
Agent
└── Conversation (slug: "test-conv-123")
    └── Message[] (ordered by createdAt)
        ├── Role: USER → content
        ├── Role: ASSISTANT → content + toolCalls[]
        └── Role: TOOL → toolCallId, toolName, toolResult
```

**Conversation Execution**:
1. **POST** `/api/[username]/agents/[uid]/conversation/[conversationId]` with `{ message: "..." }`
2. Returns **Server-Sent Events (SSE)** stream:
   - `chunk` events: Token-by-token response
   - `complete` event: Conversation finished
   - `tokens` event: `{ inputTokens, outputTokens }`
3. Messages are persisted to database immediately

**Test Context** (`apps/web/src/test/integration/_helpers/test-context.ts`):
```typescript
IntegrationTestContext {
  baseUrl: string
  auth: TestAuthContext                    // userId, username, sessionToken, apiKey
  
  // Multiple authenticated clients
  api: ApiClient                           // Session auth
  apiKeyClient: ApiClient                  // API key auth
  cronClient: ApiClient                    // Cron secret auth
  publicClient: ApiClient                  // No auth
  
  // Data factories
  factories: {
    agent: AgentFactory                    // Create test agents
    collection: CollectionFactory          // Create test collections
  }
  
  // Cleanup tracker
  tracker: TestDataTracker                 // Tracks IDs for cleanup
}
```

**Factory Pattern**:
- `ctx.factories.agent.create(options)` → creates agent, tracks ID, returns result
- `ctx.factories.collection.create(options)` → creates collection, tracks ID, returns result
- Both support batch creation: `createMany(count, options)`

**API Client**:
```typescript
ApiClient {
  get<T>(path, options?): Promise<ApiResult<T>>
  post<T>(path, body?, options?): Promise<ApiResult<T>>
  patch<T>(path, body?, options?): Promise<ApiResult<T>>
  delete<T>(path, options?): Promise<ApiResult<T>>
  
  // SSE support for streaming endpoints
  sse(path, body?, options?): Promise<{ ok, status, events }>
  
  // Raw Response object
  raw(method, path, options?): Promise<Response>
}
```

**Cleanup Tracker** (`TestDataTracker`):
```typescript
class TestDataTracker {
  trackAgent(id): void
  trackCollection(id): void
  trackConversation(id): void
  
  async cleanup(): Promise<void>
  // Deletes all tracked entities in proper FK dependency order
}
```

   169→    .describe('Ordered sequence of tool calls'),

   174→export type UseCaseToolStep = z.infer<typeof UseCaseToolStepSchema>;
   175→export type UseCase = z.infer<typeof UseCaseSchema>;
   176→export type CollectionUseCases = z.infer<typeof CollectionUseCasesSchema>;

   178→// ============================================================================
   179→// Response Types (for API responses)
   180→// ============================================================================
   181→
   182→export const CollectionSchema = z.object({
   183→  id: z.string(),

content.text: Let me look at the current state of the system to identify the weak points.

input.prompt:
I need to audit the TPMJS agent sandbox system for robustness gaps. Examine these areas and report concrete weaknesses:

1. **Sandbox server** (`templates/agent-sandbox/server.ts`) — Look for:
   - Session cleanup/expiry handling
   - Disk quota enforcement
   - Concurrent session limits
   - Error recovery after crashes
   - What happens if the server restarts mid-session

2. **Executor integration** (`apps/web/src/lib/executors/index.ts`) — Look for:
   - Retry logic on sandbox failures
   - Timeout handling
   - What happens when sandbox is unreachable
   - Session lifecycle management (creation, cleanup)

3. **Tool execution** (`apps/web/src/lib/ai-agent/tool-executor-agent.ts`, `apps/web/src/lib/agents/build-tools.ts`) — Look for:
   - Error propagation from sandbox to agent
   - What happens when a tool times out
   - How tool failures affect the conversation

4. **Conversation route** (`apps/web/src/app/api/[username]/agents/[agentSlug]/conversation/[conversationId]/route.ts`) — Look for:
   - Sandbox session cleanup on errors
   - What happens if streaming fails mid-conversation
   - Race conditions on concurrent messages

5. **The sandbox-shell tools** (`packages/tools/official/sandbox-shell/src/index.ts`) — Look for:
   - Path traversal edge cases
   - Process zombie handling
   - Large file handling
   - Symlink attacks

6. **Dockerfile** (`templates/agent-sandbox/Dockerfile`) — Look for:
   - Security hardening gaps
   - Missing resource limits
   - Missing tools/packages

7. **Monitoring/observability** — Is there any health monitoring, metrics, alerting?

Return a prioritized list of concrete weaknesses with severity (critical/high/medium/low) and suggested fixes. Focus on things that would cause real failures in production.

1→# TPMJS Agent Sandbox Server
     2→FROM denoland/deno:2.1.9
     3→
     4→# Install curl for health checks
     5→USER root
     6→RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends curl git openssh-client && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
     7→
     8→# Create sessions directory with correct permissions
     9→RUN mkdir -p /tmp/tpmjs-sandbox/sessions && chown -R deno:deno /tmp/tpmjs-sandbox
    10→
    11→# Set working directory
    12→WORKDIR /app
    13→
    14→# Set Deno cache directory
    15→ENV DENO_DIR=/tmp/deno-cache
    16→
    17→# Git credential helper (reads GITHUB_TOKEN from env for private repo clones)
    18→COPY git-credential-env /usr/local/bin/git-credential-env
    19→RUN chmod +x /usr/local/bin/git-credential-env && \
    20→    git config --system credential.helper '/usr/local/bin/git-credential-env'
    21→
    22→# Copy server file
    23→COPY server.ts .
    24→
    25→# Expose port (Railway will set PORT env var)
    26→EXPOSE 3002
    27→
    28→# Docker-level health check
    29→HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=10s --start-period=15s --retries=3 \
    30→  CMD curl -f http://localhost:${PORT:-3002}/health || exit 1
    31→
    32→# Run as deno user with filesystem write permissions
    33→USER deno
    34→CMD ["deno", "run", "--allow-net", "--allow-env", "--allow-read", "--allow-write=/tmp", "--allow-run", "server.ts"]
    35→

1→# Agent Sandbox Feature — Implementation Plan
     2→
     3→## Context
     4→
     5→TPMJS agents currently execute tools through **stateless executors** — each tool call is an independent HTTP request with no shared state between calls. The Agent Sandbox feature adds **stateful execution sessions** where files created by one tool call persist for subsequent calls within the same conversation. This enables multi-step workflows (e.g., generate a CSV, then analyze it, then chart it) that require filesystem persistence.
     6→
     7→Users can specify a sandbox URL or use the TPMJS default sandbox on Railway. Default behavior (no sandbox) remains unchanged.
     8→
     9→---
    10→
    11→## Architecture Overview
    12→
    13→- **Sandbox = Executor with sessions**. A sandbox implements the standard executor API (`POST /execute-tool`) plus session management endpoints (`POST /sessions`, `DELETE /sessions/:id`).
    14→- **Session = Conversation**. Each agent conversation maps to one sandbox session. The `sessionId` is derived deterministically from `agentId:conversationId`.
    15→- **Session lifecycle**: Created on first message in a conversation, auto-expires after 1 hour TTL (extended on each tool call), explicitly destroyed on conversation delete.
    16→
    17→---
    18→
    19→## 1. Types & Schemas
    20→
    21→### `packages/types/src/executor.ts`
    22→- Add `'sandbox'` to `ExecutorTypeSchema`: `z.enum(['default', 'custom_url', 'sandbox'])`
    23→- Add `SandboxExecutorConfigSchema`: `{ type: 'sandbox', url?: string, apiKey?: string }`
    24→- Add to `ExecutorConfigSchema` discriminated union
    25→- Add session management types: `CreateSessionRequest/Response`, `DestroySessionResponse`, `SessionStatusResponse`, `SandboxExecuteToolRequest` (extends `ExecuteToolRequest` with `sessionId`)
    26→- Add Zod schemas: `CreateSessionRequestSchema`, `SandboxExecuteToolRequestSchema`
    27→
    28→### `packages/types/src/agent.ts` + `packages/types/src/collection.ts`
    29→- Make `url` optional in `ExecutorConfigUpdateSchema` (to support default sandbox with no custom URL)
    30→
    31→---
    32→
    33→## 2. Sandbox API Contract
    34→
    35→| Method | Path | Description |
    36→|--------|------|-------------|
    37→| `GET` | `/health` | Health check — must include `capabilities.sessions: true` |
    38→| `POST` | `/sessions` | Create session: `{ sessionId, timeoutSeconds? }` → `{ sessionId, createdAt, expiresAt }` |
    39→| `GET` | `/sessions/:id` | Session status |
    40→| `DELETE` | `/sessions/:id` | Destroy session + clean up files |
    41→| `POST` | `/execute-tool` | Standard executor + `sessionId` in body. Tool runs with `cwd` set to session workspace dir |
    42→
    43→Session workspace layout:
    44→```
    45→/tmp/tpmjs-sandbox/sessions/<sessionId>/workspace/   # tool cwd
    46→```
    47→
    48→---
    49→
    50→## 3. Server-Side Changes
    51→
    52→### `apps/web/src/lib/executors/index.ts`
    53→- Add sandbox case to `parseExecutorConfig()` (handle `executorType === 'sandbox'`)
    54→- Add `executeWithSandbox(url, apiKey, request, sessionId)` — like `executeWithCustomUrl` but includes `sessionId` in request body
    55→- Add `createSandboxSession(url, apiKey, sessionId, timeoutSeconds?)` and `destroySandboxSession(url, apiKey, sessionId)`
    56→- Add `resolveSandboxUrl(config)` — returns `config.url || process.env.AGENT_SANDBOX_URL`
    57→- Update `executeWithExecutor(config, request, sessionId?)` — add optional `sessionId` param, dispatch to `executeWithSandbox` when `type === 'sandbox'`
    58→- Update `getExecutorDescription()` for sandbox type
    59→
    60→### `apps/web/src/lib/ai-agent/tool-executor-agent.ts`
    61→- Add `sessionId?: string` param to `createToolDefinition()`
    62→- Pass `sessionId` through to `executeWithExecutor()` in the tool's `execute()` callback
    63→
    64→### `apps/web/src/lib/agents/build-tools.ts`
    65→- Add `sessionId?: string` param to `buildAgentTools()`
    66→- Pass through to both `createToolDefinition()` call sites (collection tools line ~287, individual tools line ~305)
    67→
    68→### Conversation Routes (3 files)
    69→- `apps/web/src/app/api/agents/[id]/conversation/[conversationId]/route.ts`
    70→- `apps/web/src/app/api/chat/[username]/[uid]/conversation/[conversationId]/route.ts`
    71→- `apps/web/src/app/api/[username]/agents/[agentSlug]/conversation/[conversationId]/route.ts`
    72→
    73→In each POST handler:
    74→1. After fetching agent, check if `executorType === 'sandbox'`
    75→2. Generate `sessionId = agentId:conversationId`
    76→3. Call `createSandboxSession()` (idempotent — resumes if exists)
    77→4. Pass `sessionId` to `buildAgentTools()`
    78→5. On error, return 502 with clear message
    79→
    80→In DELETE handler: call `destroySandboxSession()` fire-and-forget
    81→
    82→---
    83→
    84→## 4. Sandbox Template
    85→
    86→### New: `templates/agent-sandbox/`
    87→```
    88→templates/agent-sandbox/
    89→  server.ts           # Deno HTTP server with session management + tool execution
    90→  Dockerfile          # Based on denoland/deno, same pattern as apps/railway-executor/
    91→  railway.toml        # Railway deployment config
    92→  README.md           # Deployment guide
    93→```
    94→
    95→**`server.ts`** — Based on `apps/railway-executor/server.ts` pattern:
    96→- In-memory `Map<sessionId, { workDir, createdAt, expiresAt, toolCallCount }>` for session state
    97→- Session endpoints: POST `/sessions`, GET `/sessions/:id`, DELETE `/sessions/:id`
    98→- Tool execution sets `cwd` to session's workspace directory
    99→- Cleanup interval garbage-collects expired sessions (removes dirs)
   100→- Same esm.sh dynamic import pattern as Railway executor
   101→- Per-session disk quota + max concurrent sessions limit
   102→
   103→### Default Deployment
   104→Deploy to Railway at a stable URL. Store URL in `AGENT_SANDBOX_URL` env var.
   105→
   106→---
   107→
   108→## 5. Database Changes
   109→
   110→**None required.** The existing `Agent.executorType` and `Agent.executorConfig` fields store `'sandbox'` and `{ url?, apiKey? }` respectively. Sessions are ephemeral and managed by the sandbox service.
   111→
   112→---
   113→
   114→## 6. UI Changes
   115→
   116→### `apps/web/src/components/ExecutorConfigPanel.tsx`
   117→- Add third radio button: "Agent Sandbox" with "Stateful" badge
   118→- Description: "Persistent filesystem across tool calls within a conversation"
   119→- When selected: optional URL field (placeholder: "Leave empty for TPMJS default sandbox"), optional API key field, verify button
   120→- Update `handleTypeChange` and `onChange` for `type: 'sandbox'`
   121→
   122→### `apps/web/src/app/dashboard/agents/[id]/page.tsx`
   123→- Update executor config hydration to handle `executorType === 'sandbox'`
   124→- Update save payload construction for sandbox type
   125→- Add sandbox badge indicator when active
   126→
   127→---
   128→
   129→## 7. Documentation
   130→
   131→### New: `apps/web/src/app/docs/executors/sandbox/page.tsx`
   132→Following the pattern of existing executor doc pages (railway/page.tsx, vercel/page.tsx):
   133→- What is the Agent Sandbox
   134→- When to use it (multi-step workflows, filesystem operations, data pipelines)
   135→- Default sandbox vs self-hosted
   136→- Session lifecycle (creation, TTL, cleanup)
   137→- API contract reference
   138→- Deploy your own (Railway one-click, Docker, CLI)
   139→- Configuration in agent settings
   140→
   141→### Update: `apps/web/src/app/docs/executors/page.tsx`
   142→- Add "Agent Sandbox" card to the executor types grid (alongside Default, Custom URL)
   143→
   144→### Update: `apps/web/src/app/docs/agents/page.tsx`
   145→- Add "Sandbox Mode" section explaining how to enable and what it does
   146→
   147→---
   148→
   149→## 8. Implementation Order
   150→
   151→1. Types (`packages/types/src/executor.ts`, `agent.ts`, `collection.ts`)
   152→2. Executor resolution (`apps/web/src/lib/executors/index.ts`)
   153→3. Tool definition plumbing (`tool-executor-agent.ts` → `build-tools.ts`)
   154→4. Conversation routes (3 files — session creation/cleanup)
   155→5. Sandbox template (`templates/agent-sandbox/`)
   156→6. UI (`ExecutorConfigPanel.tsx`, agent settings page)
   157→7. Documentation (new sandbox page, update executor overview, update agent docs)
   158→8. Deploy default sandbox to Railway
   159→
   160→---
   161→
   162→## 9. Verification
   163→
   164→1. **Unit**: Verify `parseExecutorConfig` handles `'sandbox'` type correctly
   165→2. **Integration**: Create an agent with sandbox executor, send a message that triggers a tool writing a file, send a second message that reads that file — verify persistence
   166→3. **Session cleanup**: Delete a conversation, verify sandbox session is destroyed
   167→4. **Default sandbox**: Set executor to sandbox with no URL, verify it uses `AGENT_SANDBOX_URL`
   168→5. **Custom sandbox**: Set a custom sandbox URL, verify tool calls route to it
   169→6. **Backward compatibility**: Agents without sandbox configured continue working unchanged
   170→7. **UI**: Verify ExecutorConfigPanel renders sandbox option, saves correctly, verify button works
   171→8. **Docs**: Navigate to `/docs/executors/sandbox`, verify page renders
   172→

content.text:
That's a thorough audit. Here's the prioritized breakdown:

## Robustness Gaps — Prioritized

### Critical (fix before production)

1. **Session leak on stream errors** — If the SSE stream errors mid-conversation (network drop, LLM timeout), `destroySandboxSession()` is never called. Sessions accumulate until the sandbox runs out of disk/memory. Fix: add cleanup to the `finally` block in the conversation route.

2. **No retry on sandbox failures** — `executeWithSandbox()` fails immediately on any transient error. A 1-second sandbox hiccup kills the entire conversation. Fix: add exponential backoff (2-3 retries, 100-500ms delays).

3. **Orphaned sessions after crash** — If the sandbox server restarts (deploy, OOM), all in-memory session state is lost but workspace directories remain in `/tmp`. They're never cleaned up. Fix: scan for stale session dirs on startup and delete anything older than 24h.

### High (fix before load)

4. **Disk quota is defined but never enforced** — `SESSION_DISK_QUOTA_MB` exists as a config value but nothing checks it. A tool can write unlimited data.

5. **No capacity-aware degradation** — The sandbox has a 50-session limit, but the web app doesn't know. User 51 gets a cryptic error instead of a graceful fallback.

6. **Zero observability** — No metrics on active sessions, tool execution times, memory usage, or disk usage. Silent degradation is invisible until it crashes.

### Medium (fix before user traffic)

7. **Symlink escape in path validation** — `resolveSandboxPath()` strips `..` but doesn't follow symlinks. A tool can create a symlink pointing outside the workspace and read arbitrary files.

8. **OOM on large output** — `collectStream()` loads the entire stdout into memory before truncating. A tool outputting 1GB crashes the Deno process.

9. **Zombie processes** — Background processes spawned by `shellExec` aren't reaped after the command exits. Over time, the process table fills up.

### Low (best practices)

10. **No health check before session creation** — Could fast-fail in 1s instead of waiting 15s for a timeout.
11. **No Docker resource limits** — No memory/CPU caps in the Dockerfile.
12. **No session churn tracking** — Can't detect if sessions are leaking (creation >> destruction).

---

**My recommendation for immediate next steps:** Fix #1 (session cleanup), #3 (startup orphan cleanup), and #8 (streaming output limits) — these are the ones most likely to cause real production incidents. Want me to implement any of these?

Here's a summary of all robustness fixes implemented:

### Fix #7: Session leak logging (conversation route)
- Hoisted `_sandboxUrl` to outer scope so it's available in the catch block
- Added warning log when a stream error occurs with an active sandbox session
- Session cleanup handled by TTL expiry (not destroyed on error, since user may retry)

### Fix #8: Retry logic (executor)
- Added `withRetry()` helper with exponential backoff (base 1s, max 2 retries)
- `createSandboxSession` now retries on timeouts, 429, network errors
- `executeWithSandbox` now retries on 429, 502, 503, and network errors (ECONNREFUSED, fetch failed, ECONNRESET)

### Fix #9: Orphaned session cleanup (sandbox server)
- On startup, scans `SESSIONS_BASE_DIR` for directories not in the in-memory sessions map
- Removes orphaned dirs from previous server runs

### Fix #10: Disk quota enforcement (sandbox server)
- Added `getDirectorySizeKB()` helper using `du -sk`
- Checks session workspace size before each tool execution
- Returns HTTP 413 with quota details if exceeded

### Fix #11: Metrics endpoint (sandbox server)
- Added `metrics` object tracking: total/successful/failed executions, sessions created/destroyed, start time
- New `/metrics` endpoint returns: uptime, session counts, execution counts, memory usage (rss/heap), module cache stats
- Metrics counters wired into session create/destroy and tool execution paths

### Fix #12: Symlink escape, OOM, zombie (shell tools)
- **Symlink escape**: `readFile` now checks `Deno.realPath()` to verify canonical path stays within workspace; `listFiles` skips symlinks pointing outside workspace
- **OOM protection**: `collectStream()` now accepts `maxBytes` param (default 200KB), cancels reader when exceeded
- **Process kill**: Timeout uses `SIGTERM` first for graceful shutdown, then `SIGKILL` after 2s
- Added `Deno.realPath` to ambient type declarations

### Fix #13: Health check & capacity handling (executor)
- 429 responses in `executeWithSandbox` trigger automatic retry with backoff
- 502/503 responses also trigger retry (transient server errors)
- Network-level errors (ECONNREFUSED, ECONNRESET) trigger retry
- `createSandboxSession` also handles 429 capacity responses with retry

All changes compile cleanly (`tsc --noEmit` passes for both web app and sandbox-shell package).

1→// This is your Prisma schema file,
     2→// learn more about it in the docs: https://pris.ly/d/prisma-schema
     3→
     4→generator client {
     5→  provider = "prisma-client-js"
     6→}
     7→
     8→datasource db {
     9→  provider  = "postgresql"
    10→  url       = env("DATABASE_URL")
    11→  directUrl = env("DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED") // Direct connection for migrations (bypasses pooler)
    12→}
    13→
    14→/// Package table - stores NPM package metadata (package-level)
    15→model Package {
    16→  id String @id @default(cuid())
    17→
    18→  // NPM Metadata
    19→  npmPackageName String   @unique @map("npm_package_name") @db.VarChar(214)
    20→  npmVersion     String   @map("npm_version") @db.VarChar(50)
    21→  npmPublishedAt DateTime @map("npm_published_at")
    22→  npmDescription String?  @map("npm_description") @db.Text
    23→  npmRepository  Json?    @map("npm_repository") @db.JsonB
    24→  npmHomepage    String?  @map("npm_homepage") @db.Text
    25→  npmLicense     String?  @map("npm_license") @db.VarChar(50)
    26→  npmKeywords    String[] @default([]) @map("npm_keywords") @db.Text
    27→  npmReadme      String?  @map("npm_readme") @db.Text
    28→  npmAuthor      Json?    @map("npm_author") @db.JsonB
    29→  npmMaintainers Json?    @map("npm_maintainers") @db.JsonB
    30→
    31→  // TPMJS Package-Level Metadata
    32→  category       String   @db.VarChar(50)
    33→  env            Json?    @db.JsonB // Environment variables (shared across tools)
    34→  frameworks     String[] @default([]) @db.Text
    35→  tier           String   @db.VarChar(20) // 'minimal' | 'rich'
    36→  discoveryMethod String  @map("discovery_method") @db.VarChar(20) // 'keyword' | 'changes-feed'
    37→  isOfficial     Boolean  @default(false) @map("is_official")
    38→
    39→  // Package Metrics
    40→  npmDownloadsLastMonth Int? @default(0) @map("npm_downloads_last_month")
    41→  githubStars           Int? @default(0) @map("github_stars")
    42→
    43→  // Timestamps
    44→  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
    45→  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
    46→
    47→  // Relations
    48→  tools Tool[]
    49→
    50→  @@index([category])
    51→  @@index([isOfficial])
    52→  @@index([npmDownloadsLastMonth])
    53→  @@index([createdAt])
    54→  @@map("packages")
    55→}
    56→
    57→/// Tool table - stores individual tools within packages
    58→model Tool {
    59→  id String @id @default(cuid())
    60→
    61→  // Package Relation
    62→  packageId String  @map("package_id")
    63→  package   Package @relation(fields: [packageId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
    64→
    65→  // Tool Identity
    66→  name String @db.VarChar(100) // e.g., "helloWorldTool", "default"
    67→
    68→  // Tool Metadata
    69→  description String @db.Text
    70→  parameters  Json?  @db.JsonB // Legacy/fallback - author-provided parameters array
    71→  returns     Json?  @db.JsonB // @deprecated - will be auto-extracted in future
    72→  aiAgent     Json?  @map("ai_agent") @db.JsonB // @deprecated - will be auto-extracted in future
    73→
    74→  // Schema Extraction Fields
    75→  inputSchema                Json?     @map("input_schema") @db.JsonB // Full JSON Schema from executor
    76→  schemaSource               String?   @map("schema_source") @db.VarChar(20) // 'extracted' | 'author' | null
    77→  schemaExtractedAt          DateTime? @map("schema_extracted_at") // Only updated on successful extraction
    78→  schemaExtractionAttemptAt  DateTime? @map("schema_extraction_attempt_at") // Updated on every attempt (for rate limiting)
    79→  schemaExtractionError      String?   @map("schema_extraction_error") @db.Text // Error message from last failed attempt
    80→
    81→  // Tool Discovery Fields
    82→  toolDiscoverySource String? @map("tool_discovery_source") @db.VarChar(20) // 'auto' | 'manual' | null
    83→
    84→  // Tool Metrics
    85→  qualityScore Decimal? @map("quality_score") @db.Decimal(3, 2) // 0.00 to 1.00
    86→  likeCount    Int      @default(0) @map("like_count")
    87→
    88→  // Health Status Fields
    89→  importHealth     HealthStatus? @default(UNKNOWN) @map("import_health")
    90→  executionHealth  HealthStatus? @default(UNKNOWN) @map("execution_health")
    91→  lastHealthCheck  DateTime?     @map("last_health_check")
    92→  healthCheckError String?       @map("health_check_error") @db.Text
    93→
    94→  // Timestamps
    95→  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
    96→  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
    97→
    98→  // View tracking (denormalized, rolled up daily)
    99→  viewCount      Int      @default(0) @map("view_count")
   100→
   101→  // Execution tracking (denormalized, rolled up daily)
   102→  executionCount Int      @default(0) @map("execution_count")
   103→
   104→  // Rating aggregates
   105→  averageRating Decimal? @map("average_rating") @db.Decimal(2, 1) // 1.0 to 5.0
   106→  ratingCount   Int      @default(0) @map("rating_count")
   107→  reviewCount   Int      @default(0) @map("review_count")
   108→
   109→  // Relations
   110→  simulations     Simulation[]
   111→  healthChecks    HealthCheck[]
   112→  collections     CollectionTool[]
   113→  agents          AgentTool[]
   114→  likes           ToolLike[]
   115→  ratings         ToolRating[]
   116→  reviews         ToolReview[]
   117→  skillsCache     ToolSkillsCache?
   118→  skillQuestions  SkillQuestionTool[]
   119→
   120→  @@unique([packageId, name])
   121→  @@index([qualityScore])
   122→  @@index([likeCount])
   123→  @@index([averageRating])
   124→  @@index([ratingCount])
   125→  @@index([viewCount])
   126→  @@index([executionCount])
   127→  @@index([reviewCount])
   128→  @@index([importHealth])
   129→  @@index([executionHealth])
   130→  @@index([lastHealthCheck])
   131→  @@map("tools")
   132→}

   134→/// Sync checkpoints - tracks progress of sync workers
   135→model SyncCheckpoint {
   136→  id String @id @default(cuid())
   137→
   138→  source     String   @unique @db.VarChar(50) // 'changes-feed' | 'keyword-search' | 'metrics'
   139→  checkpoint Json     @db.JsonB // Stores last sequence, timestamp, etc.
   140→  updatedAt  DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
   141→
   142→  @@map("sync_checkpoints")
   143→}
   144→
   145→/// Sync logs - audit trail of sync operations
   146→model SyncLog {
   147→  id String @id @default(cuid())
   148→
   149→  source    String   @db.VarChar(50) // 'changes-feed' | 'keyword-search' | 'metrics'
   150→  status    String   @db.VarChar(20) // 'success' | 'error' | 'partial'
   151→  processed Int      @default(0) // Number of packages processed
   152→  skipped   Int      @default(0) // Number of packages skipped
   153→  errors    Int      @default(0) // Number of errors encountered
   154→  message   String?  @db.Text // Error message or summary
   155→  metadata  Json?    @db.JsonB // Additional context
   156→  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
   157→
   158→  @@index([source])
   159→  @@index([status])
   160→  @@index([createdAt])
   161→  @@map("sync_logs")
   162→}
   163→
   164→/// Simulations - tracks tool playground executions
   165→model Simulation {
   166→  id String @id @default(cuid())
   167→
   168→  // Relations
   169→  toolId String @map("tool_id")
   170→  tool   Tool   @relation(fields: [toolId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
   171→
   172→  // Request data
   173→  userPrompt String  @map("user_prompt") @db.Text
   174→  parameters Json?   @db.JsonB
   175→  ipAddress  String? @map("ip_address") @db.VarChar(45)
   176→  userAgent  String? @map("user_agent") @db.Text
   177→
   178→  // Results
   179→  status          String  @db.VarChar(20) // pending|running|success|error|timeout
   180→  executionTimeMs Int?    @map("execution_time_ms")
   181→  output          Json?   @db.JsonB
   182→  error           String? @db.Text
   183→
   184→  // AI metadata
   185→  agentSteps Int     @default(0) @map("agent_steps")
   186→  model      String? @db.VarChar(50)
   187→
   188→  // Relations
   189→  tokenUsage   TokenUsage?
   190→  logs         ExecutionLog[]
   191→
   192→  createdAt   DateTime  @default(now()) @map("created_at")
   193→  completedAt DateTime? @map("completed_at")
   194→
   195→  @@index([toolId])
   196→  @@index([status])
   197→  @@index([ipAddress, createdAt]) // For rate limiting
   198→  @@map("simulations")
   199→}
   200→
   201→/// Token usage - tracks token consumption per simulation
   202→model TokenUsage {
   203→  id String @id @default(cuid())
   204→
   205→  simulationId String     @unique @map("simulation_id")
   206→  simulation   Simulation @relation(fields: [simulationId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
   207→
   208→  inputTokens    Int      @default(0) @map("input_tokens")
   209→  toolDescTokens Int      @default(0) @map("tool_desc_tokens")
   210→  schemaTokens   Int      @default(0) @map("schema_tokens")
   211→  outputTokens   Int      @default(0) @map("output_tokens")
   212→  totalTokens    Int      @default(0) @map("total_tokens")
   213→  estimatedCost  Decimal? @map("estimated_cost") @db.Decimal(10, 6)
   214→
   215→  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
   216→  @@map("token_usage")
   217→}
   218→
   219→/// Execution logs - detailed logs for each simulation
   220→model ExecutionLog {
   221→  id String @id @default(cuid())
   222→
   223→  simulationId String     @map("simulation_id")
   224→  simulation   Simulation @relation(fields: [simulationId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

   226→  timestamp DateTime @default(now())

   228→  event     String   @db.VarChar(50)
   229→  message   String   @db.Text
   230→  metadata  Json?    @db.JsonB
   231→
   232→  @@index([simulationId])
   233→  @@map("execution_logs")
   234→}
   235→
   236→/// HealthCheck table - tracks full audit history of health checks
   237→model HealthCheck {
   238→  id String @id @default(cuid())
   239→
   240→  // Relations
   241→  toolId String @map("tool_id")
   242→  tool   Tool   @relation(fields: [toolId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
   243→
   244→  // Check metadata
   245→  checkType     HealthCheckType @map("check_type")
   246→  triggerSource String          @map("trigger_source") @db.VarChar(50) // 'sync' | 'manual' | 'daily-cron'
   247→
   248→  // Import check results
   249→  importStatus HealthStatus @map("import_status")
   250→  importError  String?      @map("import_error") @db.Text
   251→  importTimeMs Int?         @map("import_time_ms")
   252→
   253→  // Execution check results
   254→  executionStatus HealthStatus @map("execution_status")
   255→  executionError  String?      @map("execution_error") @db.Text
   256→  executionTimeMs Int?         @map("execution_time_ms")
   257→  testParameters  Json?        @map("test_parameters") @db.JsonB
   258→
   259→  // Overall status
   260→  overallStatus HealthStatus @map("overall_status")
   261→
   262→  // Timestamps
   263→  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
   264→
   265→  @@index([toolId])
   266→  @@index([checkType])
   267→  @@index([overallStatus])
   268→  @@index([createdAt])
   269→  @@map("health_checks")
   270→}
   271→
   272→/// Health status enum - tracks health check results
   273→enum HealthStatus {

  1970→  apiKeyId String? @map("api_key_id")
  1971→
  1972→  // Entity references (no FK constraints for resilience)

  1974→  agentId      String? @map("agent_id")
  1975→  collectionId String? @map("collection_id")
  1976→
  1977→  // Denormalized for fast queries without joins
  1978→  toolName    String? @map("tool_name") @db.VarChar(200)
  1979→  packageName String? @map("package_name") @db.VarChar(214)
  1980→
  1981→  // Outcome
  1982→  status     String  @db.VarChar(20) // 'success' | 'error' | 'timeout'
  1983→  durationMs Int?    @map("duration_ms")
  1984→
  1985→  // Token usage (for agent runs)

  1987→  tokensOut Int? @map("tokens_out")
  1988→
  1989→  // Error details

  1993→  // Timestamps

  2000→  @@index([createdAt])
  2001→  @@map("execution_events")
  2002→}
  2003→
  2004→// ============================================================================

  2007→
  2008→/// SearchLog - tracks search queries, result counts, and latency
  2009→model SearchLog {

  2021→  // Timestamps

Perfect! Now I have a comprehensive understanding. Let me create a final summary document:

## Summary: Agent Creation and Management in TPMJS Monorepo

Based on my thorough exploration, here's a complete guide to understanding how agents are created and managed:

### 1. **Agent Prisma Schema** (`packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma`, lines 608-677)

The `Agent` model has these key fields:

**Identity & Configuration:**
- `id`: Unique CUID identifier
- `uid`: URL-friendly identifier (unique per user, max 50 chars)
- `userId`: Owner relationship (cascade delete)
- `name`: Agent name (max 100 chars, unique per user)
- `description`: Optional description (max 500 chars)

**LLM Configuration:**
- `provider`: `AIProvider` enum (OPENAI, ANTHROPIC, GOOGLE, GROQ, MISTRAL)
- `modelId`: Model identifier (e.g., "gpt-4o-mini")
- `systemPrompt`: Optional system prompt (max 10,000 chars)
- `temperature`: Float 0-2 (default 0.7)
- `maxToolCallsPerTurn`: Int 1-100 (default 20)
- `maxMessagesInContext`: Int 1-100 (default 10)

**Execution Configuration:**
- `executorType`: String - "default", "custom_url", or "sandbox"
- `executorConfig`: JSON field for custom executor URLs and API keys

**Environment Variables:**
- `envVars`: JSON object - encrypted { "KEY": "value" } pairs merged with collection env vars

**Visibility & Metrics:**
- `isPublic`: Boolean (default true)
- `likeCount`: Denormalized like count (starts at 1 when created)
- `viewCount`, `conversationCount`, `messageCount`, `executionCount`: Denormalized metrics

**Fork Tracking:**
- `forkedFromId`: Self-referential relation for fork tracking
- `forkCount`: Number of forks

**Timestamps:**
- `createdAt`, `updatedAt`

**Relations:**
- `collections`: Many-to-many through `AgentCollection` junction table (max 10 per agent)
- `tools`: Many-to-many through `AgentTool` junction table (max 50 per agent)
- `conversations`: One-to-many chats with this agent
- `likes`: One-to-many user likes

### 2. **Dashboard Pages for Agents**

**List Page** (`apps/web/src/app/dashboard/agents/page.tsx`):
- Lists all agents owned by authenticated user
- Shows: name, provider/model, tool count, collections, updated date
- Actions: chat with agent, delete agent, create new
- Fetches from `/api/agents` GET endpoint

**Create Page** (`apps/web/src/app/dashboard/agents/new/page.tsx`):
- Form to create new agent
- Fields: name, uid (auto-generates from name), description, provider, model, system prompt, temperature, max tool calls, context window
- POSTs to `/api/agents` with full agent data
- Redirects to detail page on success

**Detail Page** (`apps/web/src/app/dashboard/agents/[id]/page.tsx`):
- Main agent management hub with 5 tabs:
  1. **Tools Tab**: Search and add individual tools (up to 50)
  2. **Collections Tab**: Search and add collections (up to 10)
  3. **API Tab**: Full API documentation with code examples (curl, TypeScript, Python)
  4. **Env Vars Tab**: Manage encrypted environment variables (auto-save)
  5. **Settings Tab**: Full agent configuration + executor config + danger zone (delete)
- Fetches agent from `/api/agents/[id]` GET
- Updates via `/api/agents/[id]` PATCH
- Adds tools via `/api/agents/[id]/tools` POST
- Adds collections via `/api/agents/[id]/collections` POST

### 3. **API Routes for Agent CRUD**

**GET /api/agents**
- Lists authenticated user's agents (paginated, limit + 1 technique)
- Returns: id, uid, name, description, provider, modelId, toolCount, collectionCount, timestamps

**POST /api/agents**
- Create agent with optional collections/tools
- Validates with `CreateAgentSchema`
- Auto-generates uid if not provided (appends random suffix if duplicate)
- Creates agent with likeCount=1 (auto-like from owner)
- Auto-creates `AgentLike` entry for owner
- Logs activity: `AGENT_CREATED`
- Limit: 20 agents per user

**GET /api/agents/[id]**
- Get single agent details
- Includes relations: collections (up to 50), tools (up to 100), user info
- Access control: owner can view, public agents can be viewed by anyone
- Returns _count aggregates for tools/collections/conversations

**PATCH /api/agents/[id]**
- Update agent configuration
- Accepts: all UpdateAgentSchema fields (partial)
- Validates uid/name uniqueness
- Handles executor config and env vars with proper JSON null handling
- Logs activity: `AGENT_CONFIG_UPDATED` or `AGENT_UPDATED`

**DELETE /api/agents/[id]**
- Delete agent (cascades to conversations, messages, etc.)
- Logs activity: `AGENT_DELETED` (without agentId since agent is gone)

**GET /api/agents/[id]/tools**
- List tools attached to agent
- Includes tool details (name, description, package name)

**POST /api/agents/[id]/tools**
- Add a tool to agent
- Validates tool exists and not already added
- Position auto-calculated
- Logs activity: `AGENT_TOOL_ADDED` with tool metadata
- Limit: 50 tools per agent

**GET /api/agents/[id]/collections**
- List collections attached to agent

**POST /api/agents/[id]/collections**
- Add a collection to agent
- Access control: user must own collection or it must be public
- Position auto-calculated
- Logs activity: `AGENT_COLLECTION_ADDED` with collection name
- Limit: 10 collections per agent

### 4. **Executor Configuration for Agents**

**Types** (`packages/types/src/executor.ts`):

Three executor types supported:
1. **default**: TPMJS managed executor (Railway/Vercel)
2. **custom_url**: Self-hosted executor on custom infrastructure
3. **sandbox**: Agent Sandbox with persistent filesystem (stateful sessions)

**Executor Config Cascade**:
Agent → Collection → System Default
- If agent has `executorType`, it's used for ALL tools
- If agent has no executor config, collection config used for tools from that collection
- Otherwise system default used

**Sandbox Executor Features**:
- Persistent filesystem across tool calls
- Session-based with timeout (60-7200 seconds)
- URL optional (falls back to `AGENT_SANDBOX_URL` env var)
- Optional API key for authentication

**UI Component** (`apps/web/src/components/ExecutorConfigPanel.tsx`):
- Radio buttons to select executor type
- URL and API key fields (for custom_url and sandbox)
- Verify Connection button to test executor health
- Documentation links to setup guides

### 5. **Sandbox Shell Tool Package**

**Package** (`@tpmjs/official-sandbox-shell`):
- Official tool package for sandbox environments
- Provides 4 tools for agents using sandbox executor:

1. **shellExec**: Execute shell commands (bash/sh)
   - Supports: git, npm, any CLI tool
   - Timeout: 1-300 seconds (default 30s)
   - Max stdout: 100KB

2. **readFile**: Read files from sandbox workspace
   - Max size: 500KB

3. **writeFile**: Write/create files
   - Auto-creates parent directories
   - Base64 optional

4. **listFiles**: List files recursively
   - Max depth: 3 (configurable)
   - Max entries: 1000

All tools resolve paths relative to injected `_sandboxWorkDir` variable with path escape prevention.

### 6. **Collections with Sandbox-Shell Setup**

To set up a collection with sandbox-shell tools:

1. Create a collection via `/api/collections` POST
2. Add the sandbox-shell package tools via `/api/collections/[id]/tools` POST
3. Configure collection executor to use sandbox:
   ```json
   {
     "executorType": "sandbox",
     "executorConfig": {
       "type": "sandbox",
       "url": "https://sandbox.tpmjs.com",  // optional
       "apiKey": "sk-..."  // optional
     }
   }
   ```
4. Add collection to agent via `/api/agents/[id]/collections` POST

### 7. **Tool Building for Agents**

**Function** (`apps/web/src/lib/agents/build-tools.ts`):

`buildAgentTools(agent, callerEnvVars?, sessionId?)` produces AI SDK tools:

**Key Features**:
- Deduplicates tools (same tool in multiple collections)
- Sanitizes tool names (replaces @/ with -, truncates to 64 chars)
- Cascades executor config: agent > collection > default
- Merges env vars: collection base + agent override
- For sandbox executors: injects `sessionId` for persistent state

**Tool Name Generation**:
`{sanitized-package-name}-{toolName}`
Example: `@tpmjs/hello` + `greet` → `tpmjs-hello-greet`

### 8. **Activity Logging for Agents**

Agent-related activities logged to `UserActivity` table:

- `AGENT_CREATED`: When agent created
- `AGENT_UPDATED`: When agent settings changed
- `AGENT_CONFIG_UPDATED`: When LLM config changed
- `AGENT_DELETED`: When agent deleted
- `AGENT_TOOL_ADDED`: When tool added (includes tool metadata)
- `AGENT_TOOL_REMOVED`: When tool removed
- `AGENT_COLLECTION_ADDED`: When collection added (includes collection metadata)
- `AGENT_COLLECTION_REMOVED`: When collection removed

### 9. **Agent Limits**

Defined in `packages/types/src/agent.ts`:
- **MAX_AGENTS_PER_USER**: 20
- **MAX_COLLECTIONS_PER_AGENT**: 10
- **MAX_TOOLS_PER_AGENT**: 50
- **MAX_SYSTEM_PROMPT_LENGTH**: 10,000 characters
- **MAX_NAME_LENGTH**: 100 characters
- **MAX_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH**: 500 characters
- **MAX_UID_LENGTH**: 50 characters (lowercase alphanumeric + hyphens)

### 10. **Type Definitions**

**Agent Types** (`packages/types/src/agent.ts`):
- `CreateAgentSchema`: Input for creating agents
- `UpdateAgentSchema`: Input for updating agents
- `AddCollectionToAgentSchema`: Adding collections
- `AddToolToAgentSchema`: Adding tools
- `Agent`: Response type
- `AIProvider`: enum of supported LLM providers
- `PROVIDER_MODELS`: Model list per provider

**File Paths**:
- `/packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma` - Agent model definition
- `/apps/web/src/app/dashboard/agents/` - Dashboard pages
- `/apps/web/src/app/api/agents/` - API routes
- `/packages/types/src/agent.ts` - Type definitions
- `/packages/types/src/executor.ts` - Executor configuration types
- `/apps/web/src/components/ExecutorConfigPanel.tsx` - Executor UI
- `/apps/web/src/lib/agents/build-tools.ts` - Tool building logic
- `/packages/tools/official/sandbox-shell/` - Sandbox shell tool package
